overall.takeaway: 54.8% of all orders are delivered late — that's 98,977 shipments out of 180,519 total, representing a major operational risk and customer satisfaction issue.

ship_mode.takeaway: 'First Class' has the highest late-delivery rate at 95.3%, well above the overall average of 54.8%. This mode is systematically under-resourced relative to demand and warrants immediate carrier negotiation or capacity reallocation.

region.takeaway: 'Central Africa' has the worst late-delivery rate at 58.0%, pointing to potential capacity, carrier, or geographic challenges unique to that region that require targeted intervention.

category.takeaway: Among the top-volume categories, 'Accessories' leads with 57.0% late rate. Categories likely differ in handling complexity, supplier lead times, or sourcing geography.

qty_discount.takeaway: Order quantity and discount show nearly identical distributions for late vs on-time deliveries, confirming these alone are weak predictors of delay. Delay days (real minus scheduled) is the most discriminating numeric feature.

time_trend.takeaway: Late delivery rates fluctuate over time; spikes aligned with peak seasons indicate carrier capacity is overwhelmed at predictable intervals, creating an opportunity for proactive seasonal surge planning.

correlation.takeaway: Top features correlated with late delivery risk: delay_days, Days_for_shipping_real, Days_for_shipment_scheduled (|r| = 0.78, 0.40, 0.37). These will be the highest-value inputs for the predictive model.
